references.title: Bat activity under dimmed versus full streetlights: a randomised field experiment
references.abstract: BACKGROUND: Streetlights change where bats forage, but field experiments remain few. METHODS: In this randomised field experiment, 412 lamp posts were dimmed or left at full power and bat passes were recorded with acoustic detectors for one summer.

references.title: Hedgerow lighting and bat commuting routes: a randomized trial
references.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hedgerows guide bats between roosts and feeding grounds. METHODS: We lit 280 hedgerow sections or left them dark and counted commuting bats at dusk.

references.title: Amber plus motion-sensing lamps versus amber lamps alone: a randomised field experiment
references.abstract: METHODS: This randomised experiment fitted 600 lamp posts with amber lamps, half of them with motion sensors, for 12 weeks.

references.title: Moth flight at lit and unlit field margins: a randomised, controlled experiment
references.abstract: METHODS: We fitted 64 field margins with lamps or dummy lamps for six weeks and counted moths in light traps.

references.title: Red versus white lighting for bat roosts in churches: a randomized trial
references.abstract: METHODS: In this randomized trial, 525 church roosts were lit with red or white floodlights for 12 weeks.

references.title: Garden lighting and bat sightings in the general population: a prospective survey
references.abstract: METHODS: We followed 3,214 households who recorded their garden lighting and the bats they saw each evening.
